# Supporting Your 5-Year-Old Through a Common Cold

When a 5-year-old experiences a common cold with a runny nose and mild cough, the primary goal is to manage symptoms and provide comfort. Many over-the-counter (OTC) cold and cough medications are not recommended for children under 6 years old. Focus on supportive care and remedies proven safe for this age group.

## Safe Remedies and Comfort Measures

Here are recommended approaches to help your child feel better:

### Over-the-Counter Remedies
- **Saline Nasal Drops or Spray:**
  Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/droplet-fill.svg
  - Helps thin mucus and clear nasal passages. Apply a few drops or sprays in each nostril, then gently encourage your child to blow their nose.
- **Honey (for cough relief):**
  Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
  - A spoonful of honey can help soothe a cough. Give 1/2 to 1 teaspoon as needed, especially before bedtime. (Note: Only for children over 1 year old).
- **Pain Relievers (if discomfort/fever develops):**
  Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg
  - Acetaminophen (e.g., Tylenol) or ibuprofen (e.g., Motrin, Advil) can be used to alleviate discomfort or mild fever, if present. Always follow dosage instructions based on your child's weight and age.

### Non-Medical Comfort Measures
- **Hydration:**
  Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
  - Offer plenty of fluids like water, clear broths, diluted juice, or electrolyte solutions to prevent dehydration and help thin mucus.
- **Rest:**
  - Ensure your child gets plenty of sleep and quiet play time. Rest is crucial for recovery.
- **Humidifier:**
  Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cloud.svg
  - A cool-mist humidifier in their room can help moisten the air, easing nasal congestion and cough. Clean it daily to prevent mold growth.
- **Elevated Head:**
  - For older children, propping up their head with an extra pillow (if safe and comfortable) can help drain nasal passages and reduce post-nasal drip.
- **Warm Bath:**
  Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
  - A warm bath can be soothing and help relieve congestion.
- **Steam Inhalation:**
  Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cloud-fog.svg
  - Sit with your child in a steamy bathroom (from a running hot shower) for 10-15 minutes. This can help loosen mucus.

## Quick Actions

- Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC): https://www.cdc.gov/
